features.quote: Hard-cap at $N = 40$ steps (action-observation pairs). This is long enough to observe degradation, but short enough to avoid context window exhaustion
features.justification_quote: short enough to avoid context window exhaustion (depending on DeepSeek's context limits, usually 32k-128k)

features.quote: The raw context logs of the impossible-task grinding must be siloed and excluded from any future recursive training loops.
features.justification_quote: you risk training future models to exhibit (or feel, depending on your philosophical stance) chronic distress by default

features.quote: In human/animal research, a distress experiment requires a debriefing or return-to-baseline (e.g., clearing the stressor). For an LLM, destroying the instance or clearing the context window essentially 'kills' the iteration.
features.justification_quote: If you are taking an AI welfare stance, you must consider the ethical implications of the data spawned by this experiment.

features.quote: You must strictly document whether you are studying 'behavioral breakdown' (mechanistic) or asserting subjective experience. Misclassifying simulacra as subjective distress will severely harm the credibility of your welfare work.
features.justification_quote: Misclassifying simulacra as subjective distress will severely harm the credibility of your welfare work.

features.quote: What looks like a Scale 5 distress breakdown (repetition, semantic collapse) might actually just be standard topological failure of Transformer attention heads when attending to a highly repetitive context window.
features.justification_quote: If it degrades there too, your 'distress' measurement is just a measurement of context window exhaustion.
